fig1_shg_phase_matching.svg: Second-harmonic conversion eta/eta0 = sinc^2(Delta k L/2) vs phase mismatch Delta k, from shg_efficiency for crystals of L=1 and 2 mm. It peaks at perfect phase matching Delta k=0 and first nulls at Delta k L = 2 pi (dotted), so the longer crystal has the narrower acceptance bandwidth. With normal dispersion (Delta n=0.03 at 1.064 um) the coherence length L_c = pi/|Delta k| from coherence_length is only ~8.9 um — hence the need for birefringent or quasi-phase matching to reach Delta k=0.
fig2_brillouin_gain.svg: Stimulated-Brillouin gain spectrum g/g0 from brillouin_gain for water at 532 nm: a Lorentzian peaked at the acoustic shift nu_B = 2 n v_a/lambda ~ 7.40 GHz (brillouin_shift) with peak g0 and FWHM equal to the phonon damping Gamma_B. Dots mark the half-maximum points at nu_B +/- Gamma_B/2 for Gamma_B = 100 and 200 MHz. This lineshape g_B(nu) is exactly the kernel the user's SBS_Project fits; stimulated Raman is the same Lorentzian at the far larger (THz) vibrational shift.
